title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model
grouping: One large dashed light-grey rounded container named 'OpenVLA' in big bold grey type at its top-left corner holds the whole model; the inputs (a camera photo captioned 'Input Image', a rounded grey-outlined box with the quoted command '"Put eggplant in bowl"' captioned 'Language Instruction') sit outside to the left and the output outside to the right. Thin grey elbow lines carry the inputs under the container's bottom edge: the image up into the vision encoders, the instruction into the literal prompt template 'What should the robot do to {task}? A:' and up to the tokenizer. The two vision encoders (DinoV2, SigLIP) share a dashed rounded sub-container. Numbered circles 1, 2, 3 tag vision encoder, projector and LLM.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded boxes with coloured 1-px outlines and pale fills: yellow DinoV2, blue SigLIP, green Llama Tokenizer, purple Action De-Tokenizer, and a long wide light-grey 'Llama 2 7B' bar in large type. The MLP Projector bar and the vision tokens are filled with a yellow-to-blue gradient that mixes the two encoder colours; text tokens are green pills, action tokens purple pills; short black arrows run straight up between the rows. The output is a tall bracketed column vector [Δx; Δθ; ΔGrip] labelled '7D Robot Action', with an arrow down to a dark rendered robot arm.
proposed_highlight: The whole figure is the proposed model; its name is the large bold label of the dashed container, and the numbered circles give the three components a reading order that the text can cite.
lesson: Tint each token row with the colour of what produced it - a yellow-to-blue gradient for tokens fused from two vision encoders, green for text, purple for actions - and end at a bracketed Δx/Δθ/ΔGrip vector above the robot it drives.
notes: Venue CoRL from Semantic Scholar (title match, venue_source: semantic-scholar); year 2024 = S2 year and arXiv year. layout multi-branch: image and instruction branches merge in the LLM; flow is bottom-to-top inside the container, left-to-right overall.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: training rl-offline = imitation learning on robot demonstrations

core.what: an image (via DinoV2 + SigLIP and an MLP projector) and a templated instruction (via the Llama tokenizer) become two rows of token pills side by side under one wide Llama 2 7B bar, whose output action tokens are de-tokenized into a 7D robot action

relations.form: a row of yellow-blue vision token pills and a row of green text token pills sit side by side directly under the wide Llama 2 7B bar, each pill with its own up arrow into it

bottom to top inside the dashed OpenVLA container: encoders (1), projector (2), Llama 2 7B (3), purple action pills, Action De-Tokenizer, then out to the right as a bracketed [dx; dtheta; dGrip] vector and a robot arm photo
DinoV2 (yellow) and SigLIP (blue) share a dashed sub-container, fed by one forked line from the input photo, and the MLP projector's yellow-to-blue gradient carries both their colours

inputs are drawn as data outside the container: a real kitchen-sink photo and the quoted instruction 'Put eggplant in bowl', which is inserted into the template 'What should the robot do to {task}? A:'

channels.colour: yellow = DinoV2, blue = SigLIP, yellow-to-blue gradient = their fused features and vision tokens, green = text/tokenizer, purple = action tokens and de-tokenizer, grey = the LLM
channels.shape: pills = tokens, rounded boxes = modules, wide bar = the LLM, circled numbers 1-3 = component tags
channels.line: one style of thin grey arrows for all data flow
channels.frame: dashed rounded frame = the whole OpenVLA model; inner dashed frame = the paired vision encoders

quality.strengths: Token colour traces each source through the model (the projector and vision pills inherit the yellow-blue gradient of the two encoders), the representations (token rows) are drawn between the modules that make and consume them, and inputs and output are real data: a photo, a quoted instruction, an action vector, a robot.
quality.weaknesses: The image and instruction lines take long elbowed routes down and around under the encoders and the tokenizer instead of entering directly; the action output leaves the top-right of the de-tokenizer and turns twice; the frozen/trained status of the parts is not shown.

insights.structure: One large dashed light-grey rounded container titled 'OpenVLA' holds the model; inside, DinoV2 and SigLIP share a dashed sub-container, an MLP Projector and a Llama Tokenizer sit side by side below a wide 'Llama 2 7B' bar, and an Action De-Tokenizer sits above it; numbered circles 1, 2, 3 tag encoder, projector and LLM.
insights.data: Inputs outside the left edge are a camera photo and a rounded box with a quoted instruction; tokens are rows of small pills, yellow-to-blue gradient for fused vision tokens, green for text, purple for actions; the output is a bracketed column vector [Δx; Δθ; ΔGrip] labelled '7D Robot Action' above a rendered robot arm.
insights.emphasis: The colour of each token row inherits its source (gradient mixing the two encoder colours), and the bold container title plus numbered circles name the model and its three parts.
insights.flow: Inputs enter on thin grey elbow lines that run under the container's bottom edge and turn up into the encoders and the prompt template; inside, short black arrows run bottom to top; the output exits the top right and drops down the right side to the robot.
insights.avoid: The image input line crosses the instruction line and both detour below the container, so the input routing is the hardest part to follow.

arrangement.units: one dashed rounded container for the whole model; one dashed sub-container groups the two vision encoders; other modules unframed rounded boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: real camera photo and quoted instruction in a rounded box, outside the container
